chunks: It is narrated from Zurarah ibn Aʿyun that he said:

Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام was asked about the creation of Hawwa, and it was said to him: some people among us say that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created Hawwa from Adam’s leftmost rib. So he said: “Glory be to Allah, and exalted is He far above that with a great exaltation. Does the one who says this claim that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, did not have the power to create a spouse for Adam from other than his rib, and thus give a way for the fault-finders among the people of disparagement to speak, saying that Adam was having relations with part of himself if she was from his rib? What is with these people? May Allah judge between us and them.”

Then he عليه السلام said: “Indeed, when Allah, Blessed and Exalted, created Adam عليه السلام from clay and commanded the angels, so they prostrated to him, He cast sleep upon him. Then He originated Hawwa for him and placed her in the place of the hollow that is between his hips, and that was so that the woman would be subordinate to the man. Then she began to move, so he awoke because of her movement. When he awoke, she was called to move away from him. When he looked at her, he saw a beautiful creation resembling his form, except that she was female. So he spoke to her, and she spoke to him in his language. He said to her, ‘Who are you?’ She said, ‘A creation whom Allah created, as you see.’ Adam عليه السلام then said, ‘My Lord, what is this beautiful creation whose nearness has given me comfort, and looking at whom has pleased me?’ So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said, ‘O Adam, this is My maidservant Hawwa. Do you love that she should be with you, give you comfort, speak with you, and be subject to your command?’ He said, ‘Yes, my Lord, and to You is upon me for that praise and thanks as long as I remain.’ So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said, ‘Then ask for her hand from Me, for she is My maidservant, and she is also suitable for you as a wife for desire.’ And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, cast desire upon him, and He had taught him before that knowledge of everything. So he said, ‘My Lord, I ask for her hand from You, so what is Your pleasure regarding that?’ He, Mighty and Majestic, said, ‘My pleasure is that you teach her the features of My religion.’ He said, ‘That is for You, my Lord, upon me, if You will that for me.’ He, Mighty and Majestic, said, ‘And I have indeed willed that, and I have married her to you, so draw her to yourself.’ Adam عليه السلام said to her, ‘Come toward me.’ She said to him, ‘Rather, you come toward me.’ So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded Adam عليه السلام to rise and go to her. Were it not for that, women would be the ones going to men such that they would propose themselves. So this is the story of Hawwa, may the blessings of Allah be upon her.”

As for the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “O mankind, be wary of your Lord, who created you from a single soul and created from it its mate, and spread from the two of them many men and women” — then indeed it is so.
It is narrated: “That He, Mighty and Majestic, created her spouse from her clay, and spread from the two of them many men and women.”

key_terms.أَمَتِي: My maidservant; Allah’s description of Hawwa
key_terms.خَلْقِ: creation; the bringing into existence of Hawwa
key_terms.ضِلْعِ: rib; the bodily part whose use in Hawwa’s creation is rejected here
key_terms.طِينَتِهَا: her clay; the substance mentioned in the narrated explanation
key_terms.مَعَالِمَ دِينِي: the features or teachings of My religion; the condition mentioned for divine pleasure
key_terms.نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ: a single soul; the Qur’anic origin of humankind
key_terms.ٱلسُّبَاتَ: deep sleep; the state cast upon Adam before Hawwa was created
key_terms.ٱلْقُدْرَةِ: divine power; Allah’s ability to create without limitation

ai.seo_question: Was Hawwa created from Adam’s rib according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This narration rejects the claim that Hawwa was created from Adam’s rib and instead presents her creation as a distinct act of divine power. It also links the story to the Qur’anic verse about humanity being created from a single soul and its mate, framing marriage, companionship, and the spread of humankind within divine wisdom.
